text:
id: D-0009
type: decision
title: Adopt a compact TUF-style Signed Release Root and phase-separated assurance boundary for Governance OS
status: ACTIVE
state_class: AUTHORITATIVE
created: "2026-09-17"
updated: "2026-09-17"
owner_role: human
approved_by_role: product_owner
approved_by_kind: human
supersedes: []
governed_by: [PRJ-0001, D-0002, OWNER-DIRECTIVE-0004]
affects: [D-0007, D-0008, ARCH-0001, ARCH-0002, ARCH-0003, API-0001, API-0002]
question: >
  After the forensic meta-review of the original Governance OS, candidates 4.1.2 through 4.1.5, D-0007, V-H3,
  RoT-1 revisions 1 through 7, Contract v3 and OP-1 through OP-16, what root-of-trust architecture and assurance
  boundary should govern Phase 1 without turning Governance OS into a general-purpose high-assurance supply-chain platform?
options:
  - id: A
    description: Continue CP-1 / RoT-1 as the sole Phase-1 target through another repair revision
  - id: B
    description: Adopt a separate compact TUF-style Signed Release Root with platform/admin bootstrap and R0/R1/R2/R3 lifecycle separation
chosen_option: B
rationale: |
  Governance OS is initially private, local and owner-operated on controlled machines and private repositories. The
  original mission is an agentic engineering/governance operating system with persistent governed truth, authority,
  Human Gates, CIT, task orchestration, knowledge fabric, tools/plugins, independent verification, lifecycle safety,
  Gate W and G0-G6. Release authenticity must protect those capabilities without replacing the product with a bespoke
  supply-chain proof system.

  V-H3 establishes a necessary independent source-authenticity boundary. It does not require CP-1's universal Trust
  State, custom admitter, comprehensive selector calculus, compiler/bootstrap proof or supplier cross-product at the
  Phase-1 architecture gate. A mature signed-update model supplies non-circular bootstrap, delegated release authority,
  rollback protection and bounded freshness with a smaller trusted and reviewable surface.

  The owner therefore approves the Signed Release Root direction in OWNER-DIRECTIVE-0004. The governing chain is:
  trusted platform/admin bootstrap -> pre-installed root public keys -> signed root/delegation metadata -> signed
  release/targets metadata -> one verifier for every privileged ingress -> private verified-byte staging -> atomic
  install and local high-water -> separate post-install integrity verification.

  D-0007's trust-direction rule remains active during transition. D-0008 and ARCH-0002 are retained unchanged as
  non-active CP-1 research. The new architecture lineage is ARCH-0003 and must pass a fresh R0 review before any R1
  implementation begins.
consequences:
  - "ARCH-0003 is the only current Phase-1 architecture-review candidate for release authenticity; it is PROVISIONAL and not implemented until R0 acceptance."
  - "D-0007 remains ACTIVE and is neither amended nor superseded by this decision."
  - "D-0008 and ARCH-0002 remain non-active evidence; RoT-1 revisions 1-7 and their reviews remain immutable history/high-assurance research."
  - "R0, R1, R2 and R3 are separate gates; R3 failure does not invalidate the standard product and yields STANDARD RELEASE — HIGH-ASSURANCE TOOLCHAIN PROFILE NOT CERTIFIED."
  - "The Phase-1 support envelope may trust the controlled local OS/admin/bootstrap boundary and does not claim public multi-tenant, hostile-admin or high-assurance toolchain protection."
  - "Project repositories may pin an authenticated Governance OS release but cannot create the root, release authority, Human Gate approval or machine trust policy."
  - "No runtime/kernel/CLI/capability implementation is authorised by this decision; the next action is fresh independent R0 review."
